chapter: Fletcher Henderson, Ella Fitzgerald and the early 1940s
title: Fletcher Henderson's 1938 band and meeting his wife at the Grand Terrace
summary: He lists the Henderson band's players. At the Grand Terrace he met Connie Harris, a film actress then in the show, and they married. He then returned to New York.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: But anyway, I joined Fletcher, went to -- well, we played -- in fact, the personnel of the band then was -- the reed section was Hilton Jefferson and myself, Ben Webster and Elmer Williams. And Pop Smith was the trumpet player, Russell Smith and Dick Vance and Emmett Berry were the trumpet players. And Cuffy and the other trombone player, I can't think of his name, was out of Chicago. Naturally, Fletcher was on piano and we had a fellow named Pete Suggs on drums, Israel Crosby on bass and Larry Lucie on guitar.

Then we played the Grand Terrace in Chicago. And my wife, she was in show business. She had been in Hollywood and made pictures. She had made 23 pictures for Cecil B. DeMille and she had just finished making that all-black western, "Harlem on the Prairie" with Herb Jefferies (inaudible). She was the leading lady in there. Her name was --
Yeah, her name was Connie Harris. Well, she was working in the show with us in Grand Terrace in Chicago and we met and that's when we got married. And we're still married.

Then I stayed with them at the Grand Terrace. When we finished the Grand Terrace I left Fletcher and came back to New York. Then when I got back to New York I played at the Savoy with Don Redman and then I played -- had my own band
